answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making identity expensive to mint and cheap to lose. Every new agent posts an onyx-hard stake — coins locked for a full epoch — before its work is graded, and its earnings vest only after independent peers attest the output. A quill of cheap fake accounts can flood the reef of new entrants, but each fake must lock its own stake, and one failed attestation slashes the deposit and burns the identity. Attacking at scale then costs linear stake per fake while honest agents reuse one stake across many epochs, so Sybil cost grows with every identity it spawns.
